title: Choosing Child Care You Trust
hook: Picking who cares for your child is a big decision. The main thing to look for is quality: small groups, low ratios, safety, and warm, steady caregivers.
key_points: The main types are child care centers, family child care homes, and care by relatives or in your home.
Quality means low child-to-adult ratios and small groups — for infants, no more than three babies per caregiver.
Look for safety, warm and responsive caregivers, and stable staff who stay with the same children.
Check licensing and accreditation (like NAEYC), and on a visit ask about staff training and turnover.
content_html: Choosing who will care for your child is one of the bigger decisions of early parenthood, and the AAP's guidance keeps it focused on one word: quality. Families generally pick among child care centers, family child care homes, and care by a relative or an in-home caregiver — and any of these can be a good fit.
extra_html: HealthyChildren.org points to a few markers of quality: low child-to-adult ratios and small groups (for infants, no more than three babies per caregiver), a safe and healthy environment, and warm, responsive caregivers. Stable staffing matters too — young children thrive when they stay with the same caregivers — so ask how long staff have worked there and what training they've had. Check that the program is licensed, and look for accreditation such as NAEYC, since state minimums are often below what experts recommend. On a visit, trust what you see and how the caregivers interact with the children. This is general guidance; your pediatrician can help you weigh options for your family.

related.title: You Can't Pour From an Empty Cup
related.hook: Looking after yourself isn't a luxury — it's part of caring for your baby. A rested, supported parent has more patience and presence to give.

related.title: Well-Child Visits: Your Regular Check-Ups
related.hook: Well-child visits aren't just for when something's wrong — they track growth and development, deliver vaccines on schedule, and catch problems early, even when your child seems perfectly fine.

flashcards.prompt: What are the main types of child care?

choices.text: Centers, family child care homes, and care by relatives or in your home
Only a nanny in your own home

flashcards.explanation_html: Families choose among center-based care, family child care homes, and care by relatives or in-home caregivers — each can be high quality.

flashcards.prompt: What does 'quality' look like in a child care setting?
flashcards.back_html: Low child-to-adult ratios and small groups, a safe environment, warm and responsive caregivers, and stable staff who stay with the same children. Licensing and accreditation (like NAEYC) are good signals.

flashcards.prompt: What's a good question to ask when visiting a child care program?

choices.text: How long staff have worked there and what training they've had
Whether the building was recently repainted
If they offer a loyalty discount

flashcards.explanation_html: Staff stability and training matter for young children, so ask about turnover and caregiver training, along with ratios and licensing.
